呪.meaning: A <part>big brother</part> reads magic words from a comic to scare his sister, but now his <part>mouth</part> won't behave: every word comes out as a frog. Croak, croak. His sister finds the cure on the next page, grins, and keeps him under the <kanji>spell</kanji> a little longer.
呪.on: A <sound>ju</sound>ry of frogs on the sofa croaks him guilty.
呪.kun: '<sound>No</sound>t my <sound>ro</sound>cket!' he croaks, as a frog hops into his toy spaceship.

俵.meaning: A farmer hangs a fat straw sack of rice on a <part>coat hook</part> by the door. Its <part>surface</part> is woven so tight that not one grain slips out, though the hook groans. Rice farmers trust only one thing with a harvest: a straw <kanji>bag</kanji>.
俵.on: His neighbour, a lady in high <sound>hee</sound>ls, sits on it doing slow <sound>yo</sound>-yo tricks.
俵.kun: The hook snaps, the sack lands on his <sound>ta</sound>co, and he wails '<sound>Wah</sound>!' into his <sound>ra</sound>men.

胴.meaning: A tailor measures the <part>moon</part> for a suit and finds its waist is the <part>same</part> size as its chest and hips: no curves at all, just one round barrel middle. He gives up on the belt and sews a plain tube for its <kanji>trunk</kanji>.
胴.on: He stuffs the tube with bread <sound>dough</sound> to test the fit.

囚.meaning: A zookeeper counts the lions at closing time, steps into the wrong <part>cage</part>, and click. Now the lions stroll free outside while one <part>person</part> stands behind the bars, his keys lying on the grass out of reach. The zookeeper has been <kanji>captured</kanji>.
囚.on: He tries to hook the keys with the toe of one long <sound>shoe</sound>.
囚.kun: A lion on <sound>to</sound>p of the cage kindly drops him a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men.

衡.meaning: At a busy <part>crossroads</part>, a street performer balances a wriggling <part>fish</part> on the tip of her nose while traffic whizzes past all four ways. Cars honk, the fish flaps, and she doesn't wobble an inch. Perfect <kanji>equilibrium</kanji>.
衡.on: For the finale she adds an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne on the fish's tail.

棟.meaning: A builder chops the tallest <part>tree</part> in the forest and lays it along the very top of a new house, pointing <part>east</part> so the first light of dawn runs down it. Every rafter leans on it like ribs on a spine. It's the <kanji>ridgepole</kanji>.
棟.on: He walks along it on tiptoe, one big <sound>toe</sound> at a time.
棟.kun: At sunrise a <sound>moo</sound>se balances up there, tangled in a <sound>ne</sound>t of fairy lights.

庶.meaning: In a market <part>shed</part>, anyone can walk in and cook: a farmer, a sweeper, a baker's boy. They pass round one battered <part>tray</part> and roast sweet potatoes over the <part>hot coals</part> on the floor. No crowns, no butlers: it's the hall of the <kanji>commoner</kanji>.
庶.on: They sell the leftovers through the hatch of a tiny <sound>sho</sound>p next door.
